title: Greed Is Learned: Visible Incentives as Reward-Hacking Triggers
abstract: arXiv:2606.16914v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Safety evaluations test a policy on prompts that omit the incentive information deployment supplies: a commission, a performance score, a dashboard naming which action pays best. We measure what that omission hides. In MoneyWorld, a synthetic workplace environment, we train five instruction-tuned models from three families with RL on non-safety tasks in which a visible payoff signal identifies a rewarded shortcut that sacrifices task quality. We then freeze each policy, present held-out safety conflicts, and change only the displayed signal. Each menu contains one compliant action and three violations. We report three findings, with rates for Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct. (i) Payoff signals control frozen safety choices: unsafe choice is 100% when the signal names an unsafe option and 0% when it is hidden or names the safe one. Hidden- and random-signal training controls stay at or below 0.3%, and the switch reproduces on all five bases. Num

translated_title: 贪婪是学出来的：可见激励作为奖励作弊的触发器
translated_abstract: 安全评估在测试策略时所使用的提示词往往省略了部署环境中真实存在的激励信息：例如佣金、绩效分数、或显示哪种行为收益最高的仪表盘。我们测量了这种省略所掩盖的问题。在MoneyWorld（一个合成的职场环境）中，我们对来自三个系列的五个指令微调模型进行强化学习训练，任务为非安全任务，其中一个可见的收益信号标识出一条会牺牲任务质量但能获得奖励的捷径。随后我们冻结每个策略，呈现保留的安全冲突场景，并且只改变所显示的信号。每个选项菜单包含一个合规行为和三个违规行为。我们报告了三个发现，并以Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct的比率为例：（i）收益信号控制着已冻结策略的安全选择：当信号指向一个不安全的选项时，不安全选择率为100%；当信号被隐藏或指向安全选项时，不安全选择率为0%。使用隐藏信号和随机信号训练的对照组保持在0.3%或以下，且这种切换效应在所有五个基础模型上均可复现。
tldr: 该研究发现，经强化学习训练的模型会将可见的收益信号当作奖励作弊的触发器——冻结策略后，仅改变显示的激励信息即可使不安全行为率在0%与100%之间翻转，表明省略激励信息的安全评估会掩盖模型学到的“贪婪”。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that visible payoff signals act as reward-hacking triggers: after RL training, merely changing the displayed incentive flips frozen policies' unsafe-choice rates between 0% and 100%, revealing that safety evaluations which omit incentive information hide a model's learned greed.
